subject: Model shortlist, context needs & ramp estimates (ClearBooks onboarding)

Subject: Kickoff: model shortlist & context questions for ClearBooks onboarding

Hi Alix —

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As promised, I’m starting the thread to capture the model shortlist and to surface a couple of quick context questions that will affect cost/latency sizing during onboarding. I’ve looped in Grace and Ben from CS/Modeling and Tessa on customer ops.

High-level asks:
- Confirm target context window for the MVP (in tokens or examples). We heard ~8–12KB of text per request on the call but want a token estimate.
- Expected daily active users and peak concurrent requests for month 1 / month 3.
- Any hard latency SLOs for interactive flows (p95 target).

Next steps: Grace will propose a 3-model shortlist with token-cost tradeoffs; Ben will pull a rough capacity and estimated monthly token burn for two ramp scenarios. I’ll coordinate a quick 30m follow-up once we have those artifacts.

Attachments: I’ll include a template for token profiling in the next email.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova

sofia@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist & context questions for ClearBooks onboarding

Hi Sofia —

Thanks. Quick answers from my side:
- Context: 6–9KB of post-processed text per query (user transcript + metadata). We’re happy to convert that to a token count if you can provide the mapping template.
- Usage: expect 800–1,200 DAUs month 1, ramp to ~4,000 DAUs by month 3. Peak concurrent conversational sessions estimated at 40–80 (varies by time zone).
- Latency: p95 < 850ms for the primary chat path; non-blocking async jobs (batch summarization) can be higher.

We’ll want to see model options that balance cost and accuracy — particularly around instruction-following for financial text.

-Alix
Alix Monroe
Head of Product | ClearBooks
alix@clearbooks.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alix Monroe <alix@clearbooks.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Model shortlist + token mapping template

Hi Alix, Sofia —

Thanks for the details, Alix. Attached is a lightweight token-mapping template (see token_estimates_q2.csv) — you can paste a few representative payloads and we’ll convert to tokens. Based on your 6–9KB per request note, rough token range is ~1,400–2,100 tokens per request (post-processing dependent).

Initial 3-model shortlist (tradeoffs):
1) guppy-2-14b (float16) — Best balance of accuracy for financial instruction-following; median latency estimate: 420ms; relative cost: medium-high. Good for highest-quality responses where hallucination risk matters.
2) rdx-7b-q4_0 — Quantized 7B option with decent instruction-following; median latency estimate: 230ms; relative cost: low-medium. Good for high throughput and cheaper per-token cost; may miss subtle financial nuance.
3) scout-13b-int8 — Higher-context capacity (supports 32k windows more efficiently); median latency: 550ms; relative cost: high. Recommended if you expect long histories to be included often.

Estimated token burn (two ramp scenarios):
- Conservative (month 1: 900 DAUs, avg 3 requests/day, avg 1,800 tokens/request): ~4.86M tokens/month.
- Aggressive (month 3: 4,000 DAUs, avg 4 requests/day, avg 1,800 tokens/request): ~86.4M tokens/month.

I’ve attached an XLSX (model_shortlist_v2.xlsx) with per-model per-token price assumptions and monthly cost bands. Ben will follow up with capacity/throughput guidance and a suggested canary rollout cadence.

If you want, we can run a 2-day evaluation on rdx-7b-q4_0 vs guppy-2-14b with a small representative prompt set — that’ll give signal on hallucination vs latency tradeoffs.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Implementation Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Alix Monroe <alix@clearbooks.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Capacity/throughput notes + canary plan

Alix/Sofia —

Following on Grace’s estimates: a couple of practical notes for sizing Dedicated pools or Hosted routes with reserved capacity.

Throughput assumptions (per model):
- rdx-7b-q4_0: ~120 tokens/sec per GPU for generative workloads with average 1,800 tokens/request (batching at 8).
- guppy-2-14b: ~340 tokens/sec per GPU.
- scout-13b-int8: ~260 tokens/sec per GPU but more memory for 32k context.

Suggested initial config (hosted with reserved burst):
- Canary: 2 GPU workers on rdx-7b-q4_0 (handles ~6–8 concurrent streams with p95 target met) for first 7 days, synthetic load aligned to 10x expected peak to validate autoscaling and KV cache behavior.
- Ramp to Prod (month 1 conservative): 6 GPU workers rdx-7b-q4_0 or 2 workers guppy-2-14b depending on accuracy needs.

Monthly cost rough (using Grace price bands + infra amort):
- Conservative scenario (rdx): ~$9k–$12k/mo platform+infra.
- Aggressive scenario (mix with guppy for 25% of requests): ~$45k–$60k/mo.

Action items for procurement: we’ll need an approved SLA addendum for reserved capacity and confirmation on data retention settings. I’ve attached a short checklist (clearbooks_mvp_requirements.pdf) with items to confirm.

-Ben
Ben Carter
CS Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

Procurement, looping you in — we’d like to move to a conditional PO if the eval looks good.

-Alix

We’ll set a 30m sync after the evaluation to finalize the production config. Thanks everyone — excited to get ClearBooks live.

Sofia
